title: CAPability: A Comprehensive Visual Caption Benchmark for Evaluating Both Correctness and Thoroughness
venue: NeurIPS 2025 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem that existing visual captioning benchmarks no longer adequately evaluate modern multimodal large language models (MLLMs). The authors argue that traditional caption benchmarks are limited by short ground-truth captions, sentence-level overlap metrics, and narrow evaluation scopes that miss many visual details. In response, they introduce CAPability, a benchmark designed to assess caption quality across multiple views and dimensions rather than by comparing entire sentences alone.

CAPability includes 6 views and 12 dimensions covering object-related, global-related, text-related, camera-related, temporal-related, and knowledge-related aspects. The benchmark uses nearly 11K human-annotated images and videos, with separate data collected for static and dynamic dimensions. The authors evaluate several state-of-the-art open- and closed-source MLLMs using precision, hit, and a derived know-but-cannot-tell (K¯T) metric. They also convert annotations into question-answer pairs to measure whether models can answer correctly when prompted but fail to express the same information in captions.

The paper is methodological rather than a study of students, teachers, or classrooms. Its main conclusions are that current MLLMs often achieve relatively high precision but much lower hit, indicating a gap between accurate descriptions and thorough coverage. Models also struggle especially with object counting, camera angle, camera movement, character identification, action, and some event-related captions. The benchmark is presented as a more reliable and interpretable way to assess detailed visual captioning than traditional metrics such as BLEU, CIDEr, and METEOR.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-family multimodal large language models used for visual understanding, caption generation, QA answering, and automated evaluation.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper evaluated GPT-4o and GPT-4 Turbo as part of its benchmark pipeline: GPT-4o was one of the studied MLLMs for captioning performance, GPT-4 Turbo was used to score generated captions by dimension, and GPT-4o/GPT-4 Turbo were also used in pre-annotation and QA-style evaluation workflows.

findings.finding_summary: On CAPability, GPT-4o (0806) achieved high caption precision (79.2% average) and moderate hit (56.5% average) across 13 dimensions. The paper reports that GPT-4o was the best model on precision among the evaluated systems in the closed-source group and that it excelled in recognizing camera angle, but it still showed low hit on several dimensions such as object number and character identification, indicating incomplete coverage.
findings.measure: Precision and hit on CAPability captioning benchmark

identified_tools.name: Gemini
identified_tools.description: Google's Gemini family of multimodal large language models used for visual understanding, caption generation, QA answering, and automated evaluation.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper evaluated Gemini-1.5-pro and Gemini-2.0-flash as benchmarked MLLMs for image/video captioning, and used Gemini models in the pre-annotation workflow for data preparation.

findings.finding_summary: Gemini-1.5-pro achieved the best overall hit on CAPability among closed-source models (60.4% average) and was reported as especially strong in object counting, including a 10% and 16.3% advantage in hit over the second place on image and video object-counting dimensions, respectively. The paper also notes that Gemini-1.5-pro had the lowest K2 metric (25.2%), suggesting a smaller gap between answering questions correctly and automatically expressing the same information in captions, although it still struggled on some dimensions such as character identification and action.
findings.measure: Precision, hit, QA accuracy, and K2 on CAPability

identified_tools.name: Qwen
identified_tools.description: Alibaba's Qwen-family multimodal large language models used for visual understanding, caption generation, QA answering, and automated evaluation.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper evaluated multiple Qwen model variants (Qwen2VL, Qwen2.5VL, Qwen-VL-Max, Qwen2.5-Max) as benchmarked MLLMs and also used Qwen models in the pre-annotation/merging pipeline for constructing benchmark annotations.

findings.finding_summary: Among open-source models, Qwen2.5VL achieved the best 72B-model performance on CAPability, with the highest overall hit among the 72B open-source group (53.4%) and strong precision (75.9%). The paper also reports that Qwen2.5VL-7B achieved the best precision (75.5%) and hit (48.1%) among 7B models, but all Qwen variants still showed relatively low hit on object number, character identification, action, camera movement, and event dimensions.
findings.measure: Precision and hit on CAPability captioning benchmark

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative multimodal AI/large language model systems used for image/video captioning and benchmark scoring, without reliance on a single named product.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper is a benchmark/evaluation study of modern multimodal large language models rather than an intervention study. It uses generic MLLMs for caption generation, pre-annotation, and QA conversion, and compares their strengths and weaknesses across caption dimensions.

findings.finding_summary: Across evaluated MLLMs, the paper finds a consistent gap between precision and hit: models often produce accurate captions for what they mention, but omit many annotated visual elements. The authors highlight persistent weaknesses in object number, camera angle, camera movement, character identification, and action recognition, and describe a 'know but cannot tell' phenomenon where models answer related QA correctly yet fail to express the same information automatically in captions.
findings.measure: Benchmark-level comparison of caption correctness, thoroughness, and QA/caption gap

quality_tier_rationale: This is a benchmark/evaluation paper rather than a classroom intervention study, and it does not report an empirical K-12 educational effect with a causal design. The evidence concerns model performance on captioning metrics, not educational outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports meaningful benchmark differences and identifies practical limitations of multimodal GenAI systems, but it does not quantify educational impact in K-12 classrooms. The effects are descriptive and system-level rather than outcome-based for learners.
